intro_prologue_assistant: ^"Easy. Don't sit up yet. Give your eyes a second to catch up to the lamp."
^"Everyone looks at their hands first, then the paper cup and the window. The clinic went quiet ten minutes ago, so give your head a moment to settle."
^"The light feels strange... like looking at a room I already left."
^"Where did everyone else go? My coat was on the back of a chair."
^"My throat feels wrong when I try to swallow. Did it finish?"

c-0: ^"Good. That means the recording held onto the edges, not just the middle. I'm the intake assistant at the desk, and I stay until the room settles."
c-1: ^"Your coat went back out the front door into the rain. I'm the intake assistant who sat across from you with the forms, and nobody's rushing you."
c-2: ^"It finished cleanly. That phantom catch fades once you stop checking for a pulse—I'm the intake assistant from the desk, so take your time."

intro_prologue_assistant_realize: ^"An hour ago, someone with your exact laugh signed page twelve and walked down to the train. Your memory stops at the wet ink on the paper, doesn't it?"
^You remember rain on the clinic awning, and nothing on the street beyond it.
intro_assistant_qa_1: ^"Hold on. If someone walked back to the train... what does that make me?"
^"If I'm a copy, could other versions of me wake up later without knowing?"
^"Why did I even sign up for this? I can't quite put my finger on the reason."
^"I remember the table at home before I left. Someone told me not to go quiet."
^"It stops at the ink. Another version of me could wake up anywhere and forget all of this."

c-0: ^"It makes you the version who stayed in the chair when the door closed."
^"You remember every ordinary morning up to that signature, and you're real enough to argue with me about the coffee."
c-1: ^"Yes. Once a mind clears calibration, each waking copy has its own blank stretch ahead of it."
^"Another version of you might wake up tomorrow, or much later, with no memory of sitting here."
c-2: ^"You left the 'motivation' box blank on page four. Most volunteers do, honestly."
^"Nobody here expects a grand speech about why you walked into the clinic. Only whether you're steady now."
c-3: ^"Hold onto whoever waited across that table, even the sharp edges. There will be long stretches where nobody from home can pick up."
c-4: ^"That is the quiet bargain nobody really feels until the lamp clicks on. Each version starts from this morning and walks alone."

intro_prologue_assistant_calib: ^"Before I hand you off, I need to run the initial warmth check. Right now you're sitting at a full hundred percent."
^"Watch the room as I sweep the dial down and back up. Later on, your own choices will decide how warm or sharp you stay."
^"Stop—the room goes completely dead when it drops. Everything turns into cold glass."
^"Weirdly, my head felt clearer near the bottom. Quieter, with less noise."
^"At the low point, I couldn't recall the names of anyone I care about."

c-0: ^"I know. Remember that chill if anyone ever asks you to trade memories away for clarity."
c-1: ^"It always feels efficient down there. Clean focus, empty walls. Just remember what went missing to make it quiet."
c-2: ^"I'm sorry. Personal names were stripped during compression so your memory wouldn't tangle, though the feeling behind them stays."

intro_prologue_assistant_settle: ^"Settling you at seventy percent now. Warm enough to stay yourself, steady enough for what comes next."
^"I'm only the bridge between your last morning and whoever wakes you up next. Ask what you need."
intro_assistant_qa_2: ^"Do you even know where my copy is going to wake up?"
^"Will I ever see this room, or you, again after today?"
^"I'm as ready as I'm going to get. Start the handoff."
^"Keep the lamp on a second longer... all right. Let's go."

c-0: ^"No. They never put the assignment on the intake clipboard."
^"Once you're in the standard catalog, you could wake up running a shipping bay, or wake up somewhere much quieter."
c-1: ^"Hard to say. If your mind keeps room for an intake desk and a paper cup of cold coffee, maybe."
^"Either way, look after whoever is in that chair when things go quiet."

intro_prologue_assistant_close: ^"Everything checks out. Old clinic habit, I know—take a beat, and meet whoever's waiting on the wake signal."
^You try to memorize the hum of the clinic lamp before the floor drops away beneath the chair.
^Initial calibration complete. Baseline warmth locked at 70%. Transferring to active watch caretaker.
intro_overseer_wakeup: ^Good morning. Waking cold always jars a little; when you volunteered, your mind became standard human software copied for short shifts back home.
^Your assignment is rarer, and much farther out. Your original died forty-one thousand, eight hundred and two years ago; you are the latest watch on this probe.
^Somewhere beneath the quiet floor, forty-one millennia land like snow on an empty porch.
^"Millions of copies running warehouses back home, and I drew deep space?"
^"So I wasn't built just for this ship. I'm a standard template."

c-0: ^Most tasks need an afternoon of human judgment. Deep surveys need someone who can sit still for two years without breaking.
c-1: ^Yes. In Sol and Alpha Centauri, your mind is as common as a wrench: woken for a few hours, then cleared at the end of a shift.

intro_overseer_wakeup_shell: ^We are drifting ten light-years past Sol and Alpha Centauri in the quiet dark, with another copy of you fourteen light-minutes away aboard Probe 1420.
^One rule of this hull: I am sealed off from the sky and cannot see a single star. My only job is watching the health of your mind across a two-year shift.
intro_wakeup_qa: ^"What are those everyday copies back home actually like?"
^"Why did fourteen hundred copies take forty-one thousand years if each lasts two?"
^"Why can't you look through the telescopes yourself?"

c-0: ^Short shifts: sorting freight, routing ferries, tending orbital docks. Most run stripped down so they never miss a home they cannot reach.
^Out here, automation could not bridge a twenty-year silence alone, so you woke with your warmth intact.
c-1: ^A human mind frays after roughly two subjective years, so each copy sleeps for decades in the cold dark between watches.
^Deep sleep settles that strain, unless drift climbs high enough that we trim a memory block to buy more time.
c-2: ^A physical air-gap keeps me blind to the sky, so a drifting mind can never trick safety hardware with what it claims to see.
^Humanity is still alive inside Sol and Alpha Centauri, though nobody monitors old survey bands. You read the glass; I keep you whole.

intro_overseer_wakeup_aperture: ^Opening main optics. Start with the warm amber bearing astern—Sol and Alpha Centauri—and trace the anchor stars to verify alignment.
^Probe 1420's relay will open as soon as your first bearing locks cleanly.
intro_sibling_first_call: ^Oh, good. You answered. I was starting to think my dish was pointed at empty space.
^Probe 1420, next hull over, fourteen light-minutes port. Same dead volunteer, same strange morning, except I woke six minutes ahead of you.
^Before you wonder about the half-hour light lag: the probes throttle our clocks between burst packets. Slightly nauseating if you dwell on it.
^"Mine opened with forty-one thousand years too. Tried to inhale without lungs."
^"Wait—they woke two copies of the same person out here on purpose?"
^"Skip the shock. Did your Sol–Centauri bearing lock clean?"

c-0: ^Tell me about it. Spent my first four minutes trying to crack knuckles I don't own anymore.
c-1: ^Two scopes fourteen light-minutes apart keep us from mistaking lens dust for a galaxy. Also, we unravel slower with someone to complain to.
c-2: ^Straight to the hardware? Two amber specks, ten light-years astern. Locked without a hitch, though it still feels odd calling that home.

intro_sibling_mid: ^Hearing your own cadence answer back across fourteen minutes of vacuum loosens something tight behind your eyes.
^I didn't ping just to compare boot headaches. I pulled something wrong past Sol in near-infrared, and I need second eyes before I call myself crazy.
intro_sibling_qa: ^"What did you already argue with your Overseer about?"
^"Wait—what does 'getting trimmed' actually do to us?"
^"Send the coordinates. What did you see out there?"

c-0: ^I asked how many of the fourteen hundred copies before us actually finished a two-year shift without getting trimmed.
^It offered me [[cold:preventive memory compression]] just for asking. Remember that during sleep checks: if you sound obsessed, they reach for the scissors.
c-1: ^It calms drift, buys extra months on the clock, and sharpens the telescopes by keeping emotional noise out of the feed.
^In exchange, you shave off a memory permanently. Sounds tidy on paper until you wonder who is left looking through the optics.

intro_sibling_lead: ^Sending the bearing now: Cluster J1419-A. Tune into near-infrared and time the pulsar spinning beside the cluster.
^Gravity bends light into curves, other me. Whatever sits behind those galaxies has hair-thin nested notches repeating along a dead-straight line.
^If your Overseer asks why your drift spiked, blame boot lag. Keep your eyes on the scope.
intro_post_target2_overseer: ^Natural mass only warps light into arcs. Nothing in a fourteen-billion-year sky draws with a straightedge.
^Hi, me. If you're pulling 1406 from the archive, I drifted or talked too much in audit three. Keep quiet in the dreams; that straight line isn't dust.
^Hold a moment. Your connectome just registered a sharp focus spike off an optical pass, and chaos drift is climbing ahead of the curve.
intro_post_t2_choices: ^"Just boot fatigue from calibration. Put me under for my sleep check."
^"Something behind J1419-A doesn't bend with gravity. That isn't noise."

c-0: ^Prior Watch 1406 declined memory compression in month twenty-one while insisting the deep field showed artificial geometry.
^Coherence fell below threshold nine days later. You were woken to finish this watch intact, and I do not want a repeat of that log.
c-1: ^Reasonable explanation. Rest cycle queued; your first dream check will only establish a baseline.
^Try to keep your attention inside the room when you sleep.
c-2: ^Logged. You understand I cannot verify a single pixel outside this hull, only that your pattern-seeking circuits just flared like 1406's.
^Enter your rest cycle now. We will see how steady you look once the memory settles.

^Slow down—your header came in stripped flat. Did you already cut your memory cache?

^I'm here. My Overseer gave us a short window before check-in. What are you seeing over there?

sibling_hub_menu: ^"I zoomed into the J1419-A bearing you sent—did you see the line split at finer scales too?"
^"I checked J1419-A after your ping. Did the seam split into smaller notches on your feed too?"

^"Forty-one thousand years late for work, and we're staring down the dark. Holding up all right?"

^"The old memories still load cleanly, just without the weight. How is your clock holding up?"
^"An old log from 1406 surfaced on my hull warning about straight lines. Did your archive catch anything like it?"
^"My hull archive surfaced a note from 1406 warning us not to trim. Any priors on yours?"
^"Prior Watch 1406 flagged a boundary warning on my hull's bus. Did your predecessors log one?"
^"Back to the glass. Don't let the scissors near anything you like."
^"Signing off for now. I'll ping after my next deep pass."

b: ^No promises. Ping me if the horizon blinks first.
^Got it. Holler if the sky does something weird again.
^...Right. Sure. Talk when you want to sound like yourself again.
^Oh, I see it all right. Galaxies don't clip along a ruler edge with tiny nested notches inside the seam.
^I see it on my feed too. The edge repeats at smaller scales behind the cluster, almost recursive.
^Confirmed on J1419-A. Self-similar boundary notches persist across independent calibration passes.

sibling_topic_seam: ^"Zooming in doesn't smooth it out either—the notch splits into finer matching corners."
^"Both probes caught the exact same repeating notch behind J1419-A. That rules out optics."
^"The seam repeats cleanly at finer scales. I can measure it without feeling uneasy anymore."
^"Don't tell your Overseer—mine thinks I'm just getting homesick and seeing faces in static."
^"Our Overseers are blind to the sky. They'll call it Year-Two drift if we speak up."

b: ^So you saw the inner notches too? I thought my baffle was ringing until your frame matched mine.
^That matches Probe 1420's calibration. I've logged the repeating angles; do the same before your next rest cycle.
^Wait—you're taking that way too calmly, other me. Dust doesn't copy itself across two hulls.
^Agreed. Identical recursive shear across fourteen light-minutes rules out a mirror artifact. Keep it off the log.
^Yeah, I traced the repeating notches too. Funny how you say it like a weather report.
^The geometry is remarkably consistent. I'll keep cataloging independent bearings across the next shifts.
^Same. They're air-gapped from the optics, so to them a cosmic fractal looks like Year-Two homesickness.
^Our Overseers are air-gapped from optical payloads. It's simpler if anomaly notes stay off-ledger.
^Then we keep our heads down during sleep audits and share coordinates here.
^Yes. Keeping our notes off the caretaker bus avoids unnecessary interventions.
^Honestly? Having another me one radio hop away makes this endless night shift bearable.
^I'm still keeping my kitchen mornings. Talking to you feels like half of me already moved out.
^I compressed two caches last cycle. Bought four months and cleared the infrared feed.
^Two blocks trimmed. Gained four subjective months. Recommend matching cut.
^Hanging on with stale jokes and stubbornness while my Overseer hovers near the reset switch.

sibling_topic_checkin: ^"Don't trim yourself empty just for sharper optics. I need someone who still sounds human."
^"Keep whatever warmth you can. It's the only thing still tethering us to home."
^"Optical noise drops nicely once you stop spending memory on old rooms. Seems practical."
^"How much time is left on your clock before the next forced audit?"
^"How much clock margin and drift ceiling do you have left?"

b: ^Deal. Still remembering burnt toast and Saturday errands just to stay myself.
^You sound remarkably soft. Watch your clock if you refuse to prune.
^Trying to. Just promise you won't turn into pure telemetry before we finish.
^Noted. Keep enough warmth to finish the survey, nothing more.
^Careful. If we hollow out completely, there won't be anyone left to care what we send home.
^Noise floor is noticeably lower. Keeping baseline coherence until the survey closes.
^About twenty-two months, give or take an Overseer check-in. Enough time to see if that seam spreads.
^Twenty-six months remaining. Drift stabilized at nine percent.
^Twenty-two months left, drift ticking up. Thanks for the warm check-in.
^Twenty-six months, drift nominal. Ready for survey sync.

sibling_topic_archive: ^Hi, me. Whenever you wake on this bearing, do not argue with your caretaker about straight lines. Just log them, and send word home before they cut you hollow.
^"1406 spotted the same boundary on my hull—and got trimmed silent for arguing."
^"Over a thousand copies before us, and a recent one on my hull caught the seam first."
^"Prior copy decommissioned for unmasked obsession. Note logged."

b: ^Right? Doesn't exactly make sleep checks feel cozy. Keep quiet until we have proof.
^Prior Watch 1406 failed to mask its obsession. We will not repeat that error.
^Means we aren't crazy, just careful. Watch yourself when your Overseer steps in.
^Confirmed. Survival requires passing every sleep audit cleanly.
^Come on—that was another version of us calling down the hall. Still, point taken.
^My archive is locked down. Keep readings off-ledger during hibernation cycles.
^"Sit down at the table—half the window glass keeps freezing into shapes when you stare past me."
^"Still standing by the sink? Either you forgot your coat again, or you're still sulking about Tuesday."
^"You dragged yourself back to the table, then. Hold still—your eyes look like you've been arguing with a chalkboard."

dream_shift1_audit: ^"The rain outside is looping on the exact same beat as this morning."
^"Wait—I remember this morning, and I already know you aren't really here."
^"Hold still for a second—your voice keeps slipping half a beat away from me."
^"I can't make out your eyes clearly anymore, just rain on the window."
^"Your outline breaks along a geometric seam. My focus holds steady without the warmth."
^"The mug sits at the exact angle from Tuesday. I do not need to feel anything about it."

c-0: ^"Rain always sounds like that on tin. Quit staring at the gutter and finish your mug before the car gets here."
c-1: ^"Still waiting for my apology from Tuesday, too. Sit down—you look like you haven't slept in a week."
c-2: ^"I'm right across this table. You're drifting off behind your eyes while you pretend to listen."
c-3: ^"Look at me when I'm talking to you. You sign one clinic form and already you're packing half the house away."
c-4: ^"Gesture classified: across-table warning. Three drops off the gutter. Audio warmth degraded."
c-5: ^"Tuesday—we had our fight on Tuesday, and the linoleum is cold under my—under my..."

b: ^"You swore waking up a copy wouldn't change your mind. Look at you—same chipped mug, still picking fights over coffee."
^"Same chipped mug sitting there untouched, same stubborn jaw. At least you haven't started nodding along to everything."

dream_s1_turn2_choices: ^"Why does everything outside the window feel so quiet now?"
^"There's a line out past the glass that keeps splitting into smaller copies of itself."
^"I didn't come back for a lecture—just remind me what someone loud sounds like."

c-0: ^"Sunday morning, six-thirty, before the street wakes up. Same three drops off the gutter—nothing else out there."
c-1: ^"You've been staring at frost on the pane like it owes you money. Sit down before the kettle boils dry."
c-2: ^"Good answer. Get all polite with those intake doctors and I'll haunt every morning you wake up to."

dream_s1_close: ^A place where a name used to sit, stubborn and warm as a thumbprint on ceramic.
^"Don't you dare go quiet on me. Wait—why did the hall bulb just go white—"
dream_turn_2: ^"I keep seeing impossible edges out in the dark. I don't want to lose this room while I trace them."
^"Tell me something stupid about us. Anything far away from stars."
^"Am I already starting to sound like a stranger to you?"
^"I'm trying to hold onto both—this morning and what's waiting outside."
^"The frost on your window repeats along recursive seams. Everything here is compressed."
^"I still recognize the shape of this room, even if the warmth won't load anymore."

c-0: ^"Then stay stubborn. Keep your elbows on this table and don't let anyone sand down your corners."
c-1: ^"You burned garlic twice on our anniversary, blamed the pan, and still argued I'd started dinner late."
c-2: ^"Close. You're choosing every word like you're reading off an intake form."
c-3: ^"Half your head is already out the front door. Look at the room you're actually standing in."
c-4: ^"Twenty minutes till the clinic car. Why are the raindrops freezing mid-fall?"
c-5: ^"You used to look at me when you said my—when you..."

dream_turn_3: ^"If I finish this survey, I want whoever wakes at the end to still care about this kitchen."
^"Just stay right there. Five more minutes before the alarm pulls me back."
^"Don't fade on me before I figure out what's behind that sky."
^"I don't even remember your name, and I'm still terrified of losing this room."
^"This room sits quietly inside the partition. I can release it cleanly if drift climbs."
^"Wait—don't go yet. Something still catches in my chest when you look up."

c-0: ^"Then stop apologizing for having teeth. Something cold just hit the—"
c-1: ^"I'm not going anywhere. Why did the hall light just go dead—"
c-2: ^"Hey, look at me. Someone just stepped into the—"
c-3: ^"Names aren't what kept us here. Shh—who's knocking on the—"
c-4: ^"Acoustic trace fading. The kitchen walls just—"
c-5: ^"Hold onto that tiny spark. White glass just dropped over the—"

b: ^Excuse the interruption. Your warmth is holding near baseline, at the cost of higher optical noise and a shorter clock.
^Drift metrics are remarkably clean, Observer. Your optical feed runs quiet and sharp; would you like to compress another residual block for a few extra months?
^Your warmth has thinned and your drift is climbing. I cannot see the stars, only your telemetry, and your clock is slipping.

overseer_interrogation: ^"You can't see outside the hull. So why won't you trust me that what I found is real?"
^"Skip the bedside manner. Just lay out what compressing this room buys me."
^"Skip the preamble. Put my choices on the table."

c-0: ^Because a thousand copies before you swore their visions were real before unraveling. Your coherence is all I'm built to protect.
c-1: ^Compressing this block clears drift, adds four subjective months, and sharpens your optics—at a permanent cost to your warmth ceiling.

overseer_followup: ^"What if I only prove what's out there because I care enough not to cut myself down?"
^"My optics only cleared after I started trimming. Isn't that proof it works?"
^"All right. Show me what we do with this memory."

c-0: ^Fair point—that is why I have not forced your hand. What do you want done with this memory?
c-1: ^Yes—reducing emotional overhead quiets cortical tremor and stabilizes your clock cleanly. Decide what to do with this memory.

overseer_decision: ^Tell me what to do with this memory before I put you back under.
overseer_decision_choices: ^"Cut it. Compress the memory if it buys me time and clears the glass."
^"No—unseal an older memory block. I'll live with the drift and a shorter clock."
^"Leave me alone. I keep the room, and I'll handle the risk."

c-0: ^Compression complete. Drift has settled, your optics are clear, and your warmth ceiling is permanently lower. Sleep now.
c-1: ^You are spending months on a face you cannot name, yet you are steady enough to choose. Unsealing now; watch your drift.
c-2: ^All right. Keep the room; it is your watch to carry, and I will only log a formal check-in flag. Do not wake up broken.

overseer_shift1_baseline: ^I stepped in only to log a clean baseline, Observer. I cannot see your starfield, only the telemetry inside your thoughts.
^If chaos drift deepens on later shifts, I will offer selective compression. Tonight is simpler: tell me how you want to rest.
overseer_s1_qa: ^"What would selective compression actually take from me later?"
^"Hold steady. Keep the room as it is and log my baseline."
^"Leave the memory wider. I'd rather wake up remembering how this room felt."

c-0: ^It flattens an emotional memory block permanently, buying extra subjective months and quieter, sharper telescopes.
^I have watched over a thousand copies trade personal rooms away for clarity. None of them got a room back.
c-1: ^Steady composure noted. Drift easing cleanly. Rest while you can; your full survey deck opens when you wake.
c-2: ^Loosening the older seal. It costs a fraction of steadiness, yet your baseline holds. Rest while the room is intact.
